messages:
anya: quick sync — ran a cross-family GPTQ bake with a small per-layer clipping heuristic (+0.02) to try and stabilize long-context kv drift.
matt: nice, which families did you run?
anya: Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B-v0.1, Qwen-7B. GPTQ baseline + AWQ comparison on same checkpoints.
li: any headline numbers? even rough deltas are fine.
anya: short summary: GPTQ w/ per-layer clipping reduced hallucination regressions on long-context QA; accuracy delta vs fp16: Llama -1.1%, Mistral -2.6%, Qwen -0.9%. AWQ numbers: Llama -0.6%, Mistral -1.9%, Qwen -0.7%.
sanjay: so AWQ still wins for Mistral stability, but GPTQ with the clip heuristic closed the gap a bit?
anya: yup. Also observed throughput improvements: GPTQ pipeline (our build) gave ~2.3x tokens/sec vs fp16 for Llama-13B under continuous batching. AWQ was ~1.9x in same infra.
eva: what about latency tail? any p99 regressions we should worry about for Dedicated/low-latency profile?
anya: p50 improved across the board. p95/p99 for GPTQ bumped ~5-12ms on Llama-13B due to extra kernel overhead; still within low-latency SLA on Dedicated-low-latency when we enable shallow batching. AWQ p99 similar to fp16 in most cases.
li: can you paste the run command / bakebot output?
anya: sure
bakebot: ```
run_id: crossfam-2026-03-12-clip002
cmd: bakebot run --models llama-2-13b,mistral-7b-v0.1,qwen-7b --quant gptq,awq --per_layer_clip=0.02 --eval_sets=longqa,natlang,bbh
results: see summary below
```
anya: eval highlights (delta = quant - fp16):
- longqa (context=8k): Llama GPTQ -2.0% EM, AWQ -1.1% EM
- natlang suite (instr-follow): Mistral GPTQ -2.6% accuracy, AWQ -1.9% accuracy
- bbh (reasoning): Qwen GPTQ -1.3% average, AWQ -0.8%
matt: did you track prefix/KV degradation over long sessions (chat-style)?
anya: we did a 2k-token continuation test. Llama GPTQ had ~0.9% drop in token-level next-token-accuracy after 1.5k tokens vs fp16; clipping helped reduce drift to ~0.4%.
sanjay: model artifacts? any deterministic failures or particular instruction categories where GPTQ regressed hard?
anya: mostly arithmetic/math prompts and some multi-step code synth on Mistral. Qwen had the fewest outliers. We logged top 15 regressions for each family and linked them to layer-wise quant error hotspots.
li: deployment profile recs?
anya: proposed profiles
- gp-gptq-highthroughput: for batch-y workloads, enable full GPTQ kernels + aggressive cache reuse (recommended for Dedicated)
- gp-awq-balanced: if you care about quality/regression budget and moderate throughput (good default for Hosted)
- gp-lowlatency-fp16-fallback: keep fp16 path as fallback for p99-sensitive routes; configure auto-fallback on eval-regression >= 1.5% on critical prompts
matt: any config numbers for autoscale/bs? helps ops to size.
anya: judge by tokens/sec: Llama GPTQ steady-state ~2200 toks/s per 80GB A100 equiv with batch window 15ms; AWQ ~1850 toks/s. For low-latency set batch window to 5-10ms, throughput drops ~30% but p99 improves.
eva: notes for rollout and canary?
anya: start with gp-awq-balanced on 5% of traffic for each model, monitor our eval probes (we have 200 prompt probes per model), and watch for regression alerts. If stable for 24h, widen to 25% then 100%.
li: did you save the layer-error logs and heatmaps?
anya: yes — uploaded under s3://redwood-bake/crossfam/2026-03-12/clip002 with per-layer MAE heatmaps and samples. I added a flatlist of top regressions in the run artifacts.
sanjay: thanks! can you post a short checklist for oncall and release engineers so we don't trample prod?
anya: checklist (short):
1) Canary: gp-awq-balanced 5% - run eval probes and smoke tests
2) If regression_alert >= 1.0% -> rollback to fp16 immediate
3) For GPTQ deployments, enable per-layer clipping flag and kv-cache-verify job
4) Watch p99 latency and memory foot print metrics on model pods
5) If arithmetic/code regressions appear, pin to AWQ or fp16 and create quant-bug ticket
matt: perfect. can you add a short PR to docs/ with recommended flags and perf numbers?
anya: will do today, tagging you for review @matt
bakebot: run artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-bake/crossfam/2026-03-12/clip002/summary.json :thumbsup:
li: great work — useful to have per-family nuance spelled out. thanks anya!
anya: np — followups: i'll schedule a 15min sync tomorrow to decide which profile to promote for Dedicated. if anything else pops up, drop it here.
